title: Home saunas compared: size, seats and power
description: Compare home saunas sold in the US by size, seats, voltage and circuit. Traditional and infrared, indoor and outdoor, with manufacturer specs.
heading: Which sauna fits your home?
introduction: We list home saunas sold in the US with the numbers that decide whether one fits: outside size, seats, voltage and the circuit it needs. Use the finder if you already know your space, or browse the full list.

sections.heading: Infrared or traditional?
paragraphs: Infrared cabins are the easy route. Most one- and two-person models plug into a 120-volt outlet, though some need a 20- or 30-amp circuit.

Traditional saunas heat the air with a stove. They get hotter and you can throw water on the stones, but every traditional model we list with a stated voltage needs 220 or 240 volts. Plan on an electrician.

sections.heading: Where the specs come from
paragraphs: From the manufacturers: product pages, manuals and spec sheets. If they don't state something, we leave it blank and don't copy it from a similar model. We haven't tested these saunas.
